- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.27) in recent days, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If recent sentiment is negative and price is trending upward, model often underestimates the rally — increase forecast by 3–7% to capture momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overcorrects downward — delay the correction and allow 1–2 days of lagged rebound.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–5% buffer to forecast lows.
- Mean reversion is overestimated in short-term forecasts — if forecast is 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–4% to align with historical volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage trend continuation — if sentiment is positive and price is rising, extend forecast upward by 1–3% beyond last 7-day average.
